about: How the world runs once the clock starts (milestone 4): time, influence, buildings, what computer-run nations do, wars and peace. Used by src/sim/. Money is in today's US dollars. Building effects use the same modifiers as the stats file (1500-stats.json): "+8%" changes a number by a share, "+5" adds points. Reload the page to see changes.

clock.about: One tick is one month. 'msPerMonth' is how long a month lasts at normal speed (3500 ms ≈ 42 s a year ≈ 6 hours from 1500 to the 2000s). 'speeds' are the speed buttons (× normal).

influence.about: Your influence points: what you spend to push your nation. You start with 'start' and get 'perMonth' plus 'perStability' × stability and 'perPopularity' × popularity every month (about 2–5), up to 'max'. 'costs' are what each push costs.

brushes.about: Painting the map costs influence per pixel. War goal: land of other nations you want; your nation goes after it (more likely to war with its owner, and asks for it first in a peace). Defend: your land to guard; divisions stand there and forts go there first. Develop: your land where new buildings go first. Erase gives back 'eraseRefund' of what the paint cost. 'size' are the brush sizes (pixel radius).

buildings.about: Each building has levels 1..maxLevel. A level costs 'costYears' × the nation's yearly income, × (1 + 'costGrowth' × levels it already has), so level 1 costs a year's income and level 5 five years', and takes 'months' to build. 'effects' are per level. 'needs': 'coast' = only nations with a coast can build it.

market.name: Market
market.about: Market squares, fairs and toll roads.

workshop.name: Workshop
workshop.about: Smithies, looms and mills: the factories of 1500.

school.name: School
school.about: Church schools, academies and printing shops.

growth.about: Development moves toward what the nation's stats aim for by 'developmentPerYear' points a year, plus 'perSchool' for each school level. A nation in debt (treasury below zero) gets 'debt' modifiers.

army.about: New divisions train for 'trainingMonths' months before they count. A division under 'disband' troops is broken up. Divisions you order go in a queue: up to 'queuePerMonth' are raised each month while the nation has the men, the money and the calm. Divisions are grouped into armies of about 'armySize' divisions (at most 'maxArmies' armies); new ones wait in the reserve at the capital until trained. Each army fights on one front (or stays home, guarding every front with 'homeShare' of its strength). Every front also has militia worth 'militia' of the nation's strength. A nation's own armies attack when they're 'attackOdds' times stronger than the enemy there, and dig in when they're much weaker. 'stances': what Attack, Hold and Defend do to attack, defence and losses (Hold and Defend never advance).

ai.about: What computer-run nations do. Each nation thinks once a year (each in its own month). 'buildReserve': it keeps this many months of upkeep in the treasury before building (so it doesn't build every year). 'warChance': yearly chance of starting a war at aggression 100 (it scales with aggression²). 'warOdds': it only attacks when its side is this many times stronger. 'allianceAt': relation needed to ally; 'maxAllies'. Wars are planned first: the nation masses troops for 'planMin'..'planMax' months (shown on the map), then declares war if it still looks winnable. Armies: a nation wants 'armyBoostWar' × its peacetime army at war, 'armyBoostPlan' × while planning a war, 'armyBoostThreat' × when someone plans war on it or a coalition targets it, ordering at most 'maxOrder' divisions at a time. Infamy: 'infamyPerWar' for starting a war, 'infamyPerLand' × land taken ÷ own land; 'infamyDecay' of it fades each year. Coalitions form against a neighbour with infamy from 'coalitionAt', or 'coalitionPower' × stronger than its neighbours on average, among nations whose relation with it is under 'coalitionRelation'; they declare war together when they're 'coalitionOdds' × as strong. Revolts: below 'revoltBelow' stability a nation has a monthly chance of up to 'revoltChance' (more the lower it is) that a region of 'revoltShareMin'..'revoltShareMax' of its land breaks away as a new nation, if it has 'revoltMinPixels' pixels or more and had no revolt in 'revoltCooldownYears' years.

relations.about: How much two neighbours like each other, -100..100. They start at 'base', minus 'aggression' × the two aggressions, plus 'sameIdeology' when they share one, plus up to ± 'random'. Each month they drift 'drift' of the way back to their start. A war costs 'war' a month; a peace leaves 'afterPeace'. Your pushes move them by 'push'.

war.about: Wars with front lines. Every month each side's strength is its troops × army quality ÷ 50 (defenders × (1 + defence ÷ 100)), with its allies. The war score (−100..100, + = attackers winning) moves by up to 'scorePerMonth' toward the stronger side, and each side loses about 'losses' of its troops a month (more against a stronger enemy). Along each front (two enemies whose land touches; a nation's army is split between its fronts) the stronger one pushes into the other's land: it gets 'pushRate' × the front's length (at least 'minPush') × its edge (0 when even, 1 when overwhelming) to spend on pixels, at most 'maxShare' of the loser's land a month; what it can't spend carries over to the next month, so short fronts still move. Each pixel costs 'conquestCost' by terrain, ×'defendPaintCost' on land you painted Defend. Edges under 'deadZone' don't move the front. Enemies whose land doesn't touch can still fight across up to 'seaCrossing' pixels of sea (islands, straits): the first pixels taken that way (the landing) cost 'seaCost' × as much.

peace.about: When a war ends. Everyone keeps the land they hold (fronts move during the war). Computer nations make peace when the war score reaches 'winAt' (after 'minMonths'), or after 'maxMonths' whatever it is. When YOUR nation is winning, you decide: the war goes on (and your armies keep conquering) until you make peace, or for at most twice 'maxMonths'. On top of the land, from 'tributeAt' the loser pays 'tributeShare' of its income every year for 'tributeYears' years (half that to each of the winner's allies); a loser smaller than 'annexSize' × the winner's land is taken whole from 'annexAt'.

save.about: The game saves in your browser every 'everyYears' years (and when you leave the page); the start screen then offers Continue.
